structure:
[part 1] MS CCRS Social Studies, one PDF containing two editions back to back: the 2022 edition (u1-u1641, pages 1-173) and an earlier 2021 edition (u1642 onward, pages 174+). Each edition: front matter (cover, TOC, acknowledgments, committees, introduction, strands overview of Civics/Civil Rights/Economics/Geography/History, K-8 sequencing, middle-school course-option table), then Primary Courses K-8 each with a title page (e.g. 'Grade 1 Citizenship at School' plus a note that examples are not exhaustive), then a two-column table 'Standard | Objectives'. Codes: K-3 strand-based (K.CI.1 Civics, .E. Economics, .CR. Civil Rights, .G. Geography, .H. History; e.g. 2.G.4); grade 4 theme code 4.MS.n; grades 5-8 plain numbers (5.1, 6.16, 7.9, 8.10); compacted grade 7 uses 7C.n; Carnegie-unit courses use course prefixes (MS, WH, USH, USG, E, ITG, AWG, AAS, HAME, PAD, PSY.I, PSY.II, SOC, LRE, MIN, WC). Standard text sits in column C1 and its numbered Objectives (with inline e.g. lists) in the adjacent cell; no separate example/teacher-note blocks, so objectives are labeled standards. Grade 4-8 pages carry a note 'This course contains all Social Studies Strands'. High school Carnegie-unit courses (required: Mississippi Studies, World History, US History, US Government, Economics; electives: Intro to Geography, Advanced World Geography, African American Studies, History of the Ancient Middle East, Problems of American Democracy, Psychology I/II, Sociology, Law Related Education, Minority Studies, Western Civilization) are labeled grades 9-12 with the course title. Grade labels come from the grade/course title pages and page headings.
[part 2] MS CCRS Social Studies, one PDF containing two documents. Part A (earlier units, outside this range) is the 2021 K-12 standards; within this range it continues as the 2021 high-school course tables: each course has a divider page (course title, Carnegie unit, 'Page n-m'), then a two-column table 'Standard | Objectives' repeated per page, with standard codes like USH n, USG.n, E.n, AWG.n, AAS.n, HAME.n, PAD.n, PSY.n, SOC.n, LRE.n, MIN.n, HUM.n; the standard text is in the first column cell and its numbered objectives are in the next cell (often in one merged unit). All high-school courses are Carnegie-unit courses labeled grades 9-12 with course = title as written. USH 5-12 here belong to 'US History: 1877 to Present' (course title from the divider before the range, u2529). Part B (from u3212/u3215) is a second document, the 2018 MS CCRS with 2021 redline revisions: cover, acknowledgments, introduction, five strands (Civics, Economics, Civil Rights, Geography, History), sequencing charts, then grade sections (Kindergarten ... Eighth Grade, Seventh Grade Compacted) and 2018 HS courses (Mississippi Studies, Introduction to Geography, World History: Age of Enlightenment to Present, US History: 1877 to Present, US Government, Economics). Each grade section = theme row, then per-strand tables 'STANDARD | OBJECTIVE(S)' with 2018 codes (CI.K.1, E.1.1, G.4.2, H.5.3 ...) merged in the same cell with the revised 2021 codes (K.CI.1, 4.MS.5, 5.2, 7C.6, 8.1 ...); old and revised wording and 'becomes N' / 'Reordered/Updated Objectives' are concatenated in the same cell, so units mix struck-through and inserted text. Grades 4 and 5 are followed by clean 2021 chronological versions (4.MS.n; 5.n). Every page of part B carries a repeated running header unit ('MISSISSIPPI COLLEGE- and CAREER-READINESS STANDARDS for the Social Studies - 2018') that is labeled backup. Immigration-relevant objectives sit inside the standards cells (no separate example blocks exist).
[part 3] MS (Mississippi College- and Career-Readiness Standards for the Social Studies 2018). This range (pp. 450-481) is the end of the Economics course and the high-school elective courses. Each course has a title table: course title, credit (1 or 1/2 Carnegie credit), 'STRANDS: ...' line, then a two-column table STANDARD | OBJECTIVE(S). Standard codes are course-abbreviation.number (E.6, AWG.1, PAD.1, HAME.1, AAS.1, PSY.1, SOC.1, LRE.1, MIN.1, HUM.1); column C1 holds the standard statement with '(Strands: ...)', C2 (or C3 when split by line) holds the numbered objectives. No grade is given for these courses, so grades=9-12 and course=title as written. The running header 'MISSISSIPPI COLLEGE- and CAREER-READINESS STANDARDS ...' appears as a unit on every page. Economics pages 450-452 are a redline revision with old and new text merged. Page 481 holds closing support-documents text.
